questions.q: What is the precursor to the pyramid, consisting of a rectangular flat-roofed structure with inward-sloping sides?
questions.n: These early tombs served as the structural foundation for the later evolution into stepped and true pyramids.

questions.q: Which pyramid at Dashur is known for its change in slope mid-way up, caused by structural instability during construction?
questions.n: To prevent collapse, the angle was reduced from 54 degrees to 43 degrees, resulting in its unique silhouette.

questions.q: What is the name of the limestone casing that originally covered the Great Pyramids, making them shine white in the sun?
questions.n: Quarried across the Nile, this high-quality white limestone was used to create a seamless, gleaming outer finish.

questions.q: In the Giza complex, which pyramid is the only one that still retains some of its original casing stones at the very apex?
questions.n: The remaining casing at the top gives the illusion that this pyramid is taller than the Great Pyramid.

questions.q: What is the term for the small 'offering chapel' or chamber inside a mastaba where the statue of the deceased was kept?
questions.n: The serdab allowed the Ka (spirit) of the deceased to interact with the world through small slits in the wall.

questions.q: Which church in Iloilo is famous for its pediment featuring a relief of St. Christopher carrying the Christ Child amidst coconut and papaya trees?
questions.n: The facade is a masterpiece of 'Filipino Baroque,' blending Catholic iconography with native flora.

questions.q: Which church in Ilocos Norte features 24 massive brick buttresses that flare out from the sides to protect it from earthquakes?
questions.n: The buttresses are so large they dominate the side elevations, a signature of the 'Earthquake Baroque' style.

questions.q: What is the only UNESCO Baroque church located within the walled city of Intramuros, Manila?
questions.n: Completed in 1607, it is the oldest stone church in the Philippines and features a magnificent trompe l'oeil ceiling.

questions.q: Which of the four UNESCO churches is built on a hill and served as a citadel or fortress during times of unrest?
questions.n: Unlike traditional plazas where the church is central, this one is elevated for defensive and symbolic purposes.

questions.q: What specific building material, made of coral stone and lime mortar, gives these churches their massive, heavy appearance?
questions.n: Sillar refers to a white volcanic stone, while the Philippine version often used coral stone or adobe blocks.

questions.q: Who was the first-ever recipient of the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 1979?
questions.n: A central figure in 20th-century architecture, he transitioned from the International Style to Postmodernism.

questions.q: Which Pritzker laureate is known for his minimalist 'Church of the Light' in Japan and his masterly use of exposed 'silky' concrete?
questions.n: Ando is a self-taught architect famous for his use of geometric forms and Zen-like treatment of light and space.

questions.q: Who is the first African architect to win the Pritzker Prize (2022), known for his sustainable and community-focused designs?
questions.n: Born in Burkina Faso, he is celebrated for using local materials and traditional techniques to build schools and clinics.

questions.q: Which 2000 Pritzker winner designed the Seattle Central Library and wrote the book S,M,L,XL?
questions.n: A provocative theorist and architect, Koolhaas is the founder of OMA (Office for Metropolitan Architecture).

questions.q: Name the Swiss duo who won the Pritzker in 2001, famous for the Bird’s Nest Stadium in Beijing and the Tate Modern in London.
questions.n: Jacques Herzog and Pierre de Meuron are known for their innovative use of materials and facade treatments.

questions.q: What is the name of the slight outward curve (swelling) of the column shaft used to counteract the optical illusion of concavity?
questions.n: This refinement makes the columns appear straight and strong under the weight of the entablature.

questions.q: What is the term for the decorative border or 'key pattern' frequently found in the friezes of Greek temples?
questions.n: This geometric pattern is composed of a continuous line, shaped into a repeated motif.

questions.q: In the Doric Order, what are the vertical channels or grooves carved into the column shaft called?
questions.n: Fluting creates a play of light and shadow that emphasizes the verticality and roundness of the column.

questions.q: What do you call the triangular gable at the end of a pitched roof, usually filled with sculptural reliefs?
questions.n: The pediment is the crowning element of the Greek temple facade, depicting mythological scenes.

questions.q: What is the Crepidoma in a Greek temple?
questions.n: It usually consists of three steps, elevating the temple above the surrounding ground.

questions.q: The National Museum of Natural History in Manila is a famous example of adaptive reuse. What was the building's original function?
o: Department of Agriculture and Commerce Building
questions.n: Designed by Antonio Toledo, it was adapted into a museum featuring the iconic 'Tree of Life' structure in its courtyard.

questions.q: What is the name of the high-line park in New York City that was repurposed from an abandoned elevated railway?
questions.n: This project revitalized the West Side of Manhattan and became a global model for post-industrial urban renewal.

questions.q: The First United Building in Escolta is a hub for creative start-ups today. What was its original name and primary function?
questions.n: Designed by Andres Luna de San Pedro, this Art Deco landmark was originally a high-end office and commercial building.

questions.q: What is the term for the careful restoration of a building’s exterior while completely gutting and modernizing the interior?
questions.n: This controversial practice preserves the streetscape while allowing for modern spatial requirements inside.

questions.q: In adaptive reuse, what is the term for a building that is protected by law due to its historical or cultural significance, preventing it from being demolished?
questions.n: Legal designations like this ensure that the architectural and historical value of a building is maintained for future generations.
